messages:
maya: Heads up — scheduler alerts in us-west-2. Queue for short-jobs spiked, but a bunch of GPUs are idle. Looks like requests are stuck at the head and nothing is getting scheduled. @tony @linh can you take a look? :warning:

sre-bot: [ALERT] 2026-03-21T12:09:30Z queue_length_high: channel=short-jobs region=us-west-2 value=487 threshold=200

tony: I'm on it. Any logs or quickly reproducible steps?

maya: grabbing logs now. earliest repro trace shows repeated admission failures with head_of_line markers. snippet:```
I0321 12:10:21 admission.go:234] admit failed: head_of_line_block=true queue=short-jobs node=gpux-12
I0321 12:10:21 admission.go:240] requeue_count=23 job_id=job-abc type=short
I0321 12:10:22 scheduler.go:489] assigning 0/8 gpus to job=big-batch-93 preemptable=false
I0321 12:10:22 scheduler_metrics.go:102] idle_gpus=12 running_jobs=4 pending_jobs=510
```

linh: quick hypothesis: admission controller is re-inserting a job at the head when placement fails, which prevents later higher-fit jobs from trying other nodes. seen similar pattern in older scheduler bug.

jess: I can repro locally. small test harness:```python
# simplified admission loop (test harness)
while queue:
    job = queue.pop(0)
    if not can_place(job):
        queue.insert(0, job)  # BUG: this keeps the failing job at head forever
        break
    schedule(job)
```
The real code has an optimization to avoid scanning the whole queue; that optimization causes a head-lock when placement fails for small jobs on fragmented capacity.

tony: nice catch. That reinsert-to-head optimization was added in the v2026-03-17 scheduler rollout (PR #3689) to improve latency for short jobs but it didn't account for fallback scanning.

maya: urgent plan? rollback the scheduler or patch? We need to free the blocked queue and avoid throttling client requests.

tony: I propose 2-step: 1) immediate rollback of the rollout to v2026-03-09 for the control plane in us-west-2 (canary first), 2) backport a fix that changes reinsert to append-to-tail and triggers a short exponential backoff so it doesn't spin. I'll open PR now.

jess: patch diff in test harness looks like:```diff
- queue.insert(0, job)
+ queue.append(job)  # move failing job to tail
+ job.backoff *= 2
```
Works in my local sim: throughput improves and head-of-line clears in ~30s.

linh: watchouts: moving to tail increases latency for true short jobs that repeatedly fail transiently. backoff cap needed (say 5s). also ensure metrics tag head_of_line=false after change.

maya: okay do rollback canary now for us-west-2 control-plane. notify infra-oncall and start limited rollout if green. @deploy-bot can you start the rollback canary for cluster scheduler us-west-2? :pray:

deploy-bot: Deployment request received: rollback scheduler -> v2026-03-09 for region=us-west-2. Initiating canary on cluster gpufleet-canary-3.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy complete (1855001700). Health checks: passed=12 failed=0.

tony: canary looks clean. metrics after rollback:```
curl -s http://metrics.internal/queues/us-west-2 | jq .short
{
  "head": 32,
  "running": 34,
  "idle_gpus": 10
}
```

maya: huge improvement, queues draining and GPU utilization back to normal. Good job.

jess: I'll open PR with the append/backoff fix + unit tests and a sim for fragmentation. PR will include a configurable cap and a flag for turn-on.

linh: follow-up items: postmortem, add a metric for "reinserted_head_count" and an alert for sustained head-of-line > 2m, add e2e sim for fragmentation in CI.

maya: +1. I'll file the incident and tag owners. Thanks all. :tada:
